subject.title: fix: block no-auth managed gateway LAN installs

question: Should managed Gateway install/refresh fail before service rewrite when the effective config is non-loopback plus `gateway.auth.mode: "none"`, even if an inactive token is already present?
rationale: The patch aligns install with runtime security behavior, but it can make existing invalid operator configs stop earlier during setup or refresh instead of later at Gateway startup.

options.title: Accept the earlier fail-closed install guard
options.body: Merge the narrowed preflight so invalid no-auth non-loopback managed installs stop before rewriting the service and show the remediation command.

options.title: Require fuller managed-service proof
options.body: Ask for a redacted Windows Scheduled Task or equivalent managed-service run before accepting the compatibility timing change.

options.title: Pause for broader update proof
options.body: Keep this PR paused if maintainers only want a fix after the update-mutation claim in the related closed report is reproduced.

recommendation.title: Accept the earlier fail-closed install guard
recommendation.body: Merge the narrowed preflight so invalid no-auth non-loopback managed installs stop before rewriting the service and show the remediation command.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the strongest recent and historical trail across Gateway auth hardening, runtime refusal, and service-install behavior.
